text: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married—for he had married a Cushite woman.
They said, "Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Has he not spoken through us as well?" And the LORD heard it.
Now Moses was a very humble man, more so than anyone else on the face of the earth.
Suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, "Come out, the three of you, to the tent of meeting." So the three of them went out.
Then the LORD came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent. He called Aaron and Miriam, and the two of them stepped forward.
He said, "Listen to my words: When there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, make myself known to him in a vision; I speak with him in a dream.

versions.text: He said, "Listen to my words: When a prophet of the LORD arises among you, I reveal myself to him in visions; I speak with him in dreams.
versions.explanation: In the Hebrew, the divine name is the subject of the following clause ("I, the LORD, make myself known"), not a modifier of "prophet." As rendered, the LORD is spoken of in the third person ("a prophet of the LORD") and then in the first person ("I reveal myself") within the same sentence, which is inconsistent. Also, "arises" adds an idea not in the verb hayah.

versions.text: He said, "Listen to my words: When there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, make myself known to him in visions; I speak with him in dreams.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has singular nouns with the article: בַּמַּרְאָה ("in a vision") and בַּחֲלוֹם ("in a dream"). The singular keeps the parallel tight and reads well aloud; the plural generalizes slightly beyond the source. The plural is a defensible idiomatic rendering, so it remains a legitimate alternative.

text: Not so with my servant Moses; he is faithful in all my house.
With him I speak face to face, plainly and not in riddles; he sees the form of the LORD. Why, then, were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?"
The anger of the LORD burned against them, and he departed.
When the cloud lifted from above the tent, there stood Miriam, her skin diseased, white as snow. Aaron turned toward her and saw that she was diseased.

versions.text: When the cloud lifted from above the tent, there stood Miriam, leprous, white as snow. Aaron turned toward her and saw that she was leprous.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew term does not denote modern-day leprosy (Hansen's disease) but a range of serious skin conditions rendering a person ritually unclean. A rendering such as "her skin diseased" (or keeping "leprous" with a footnote explaining the Hebrew term) avoids a medically misleading identification for listeners.

text: Aaron said to Moses, "Please, my lord, do not hold against us this sin we have so foolishly committed.
Do not let her be like a stillborn child, coming from the womb with its flesh half wasted away."
So Moses cried out to the LORD, "Please, God, heal her!"
The LORD answered Moses, "If her father had spit in her face, would she not be in disgrace for seven days? Let her be confined outside the camp for seven days; after that she may be brought back in."
So Miriam was confined outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not move on until she was brought back.
After that the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the Desert of Paran.
